title: A practical guide to CMS editorial workflows
body:
CMS editorial workflows help teams plan, draft, review, approve, and publish content with fewer handoffs.

A strong workflow defines ownership for every content stage and keeps feedback close to the draft. It also gives editors a shared checklist for accessibility, search optimization, and brand consistency before publication.

Teams can start by mapping each content type to a clear owner, reviewer, and publishing destination. The assistant can then evaluate whether a draft includes enough context, uses the expected keywords, and has a summary that works for listing pages. Editors can use the structured suggestions as a first pass before applying their own judgment.

For larger sites, the same workflow can support product updates, knowledge base articles, campaign pages, and evergreen guides. Keeping recommendations structured makes it easier to connect the assistant to a CMS queue, a scheduled audit, or a manual pre-publish checklist.

A practical rollout should also include feedback from writers, subject matter experts, and publishing managers. Their input helps tune thresholds, refine keyword guidance, and identify where automated suggestions should defer to human editorial standards.
summary: A practical overview of CMS editorial workflows for content teams.
